title: Notification — Specified Value Threshold Increase to Rs. 3 Lakhs
full_text: Government of India, Ministry of Law and Justice, Department of Legal Affairs. Notification S.O. 3550(E), dated 3rd May 2018. In exercise of the powers conferred by clause (i) of sub-section (1) of section 2 of the Commercial Courts Act, 2015 (4 of 2016), the Central Government hereby specifies that the Specified Value shall not be less than three lakh rupees. This notification effectively lowers the threshold for commercial disputes to be heard by Commercial Courts from the original amount, thereby expanding the jurisdiction of Commercial Courts to cover a wider range of commercial disputes and providing faster resolution mechanisms to more litigants. This amendment was made pursuant to the Commercial Courts, Commercial Division and Commercial Appellate Division of High Courts (Amendment) Act, 2018.

title: Notification — Pre-Institution Mediation and Settlement under Commercial Courts Act
full_text: Government of India, Ministry of Law and Justice. Notification regarding Section 12A of the Commercial Courts Act, 2015 (as amended in 2018). Section 12A mandates pre-institution mediation and settlement in commercial disputes where no urgent interim relief is contemplated. A suit which does not contemplate any urgent interim relief shall not be instituted unless the plaintiff exhausts the remedy of pre-institution mediation in accordance with such manner and procedure as may be prescribed by rules made by the Central Government. The Central Government shall, by notification, establish authorities for pre-institution mediation. The mediation process shall be completed within a period of three months from the date of application, which may be extended for a further period of two months with the consent of the parties. The process aims to reduce the burden on commercial courts by encouraging alternative dispute resolution.

title: Notification — E-Filing in Commercial Courts during COVID-19
full_text: Supreme Court of India, In Re: Guidelines for Court Functioning through Video Conferencing during COVID-19 Pandemic. The Supreme Court directed that all commercial courts shall adopt e-filing mechanisms and virtual hearings to ensure continuity of justice during the pandemic. Key guidelines include: (1) All new commercial suits above Specified Value shall be filed electronically through the e-Courts platform; (2) Case management hearings in commercial disputes may be conducted through video conferencing; (3) Written statements, affidavits, and other documents may be filed electronically with digital signatures; (4) Courts shall maintain digital records of all proceedings. This notification accelerated the digital transformation of commercial courts across India and established precedents for technology-enabled justice delivery.

title: Notification — Commercial Courts (Statistical Data) Rules, 2023
full_text: Ministry of Law and Justice, Department of Justice. Commercial Courts (Statistical Data) Rules, 2023. In exercise of the powers conferred by section 17 of the Commercial Courts Act, 2015, the Central Government hereby makes the following rules for the collection and publication of statistical data relating to commercial disputes. (1) Every Commercial Court and Commercial Division shall maintain data regarding: (a) number of cases filed, pending, and disposed; (b) average time taken for disposal; (c) nature and value of commercial disputes; (d) number of cases transferred under section 15; (e) cases where pre-institution mediation was conducted. (2) Such data shall be furnished quarterly to the National Judicial Data Grid. These rules aim to bring transparency and enable evidence-based policy making for improving the efficiency of commercial dispute resolution in India.
